checked.label: 23 in 100 (how-with-help) — not marked changed, flagged because plan step 5 was aligned to it
problems: Source timing: 'an average of 37% intervention participants achieved PPA at end of treatment, and this decreased to 24% at three to four months from baseline and to 23% at follow-up of longer than four months' (Gates 2016, PMC4914383 via NCBI BioC, refetched 2026-11-08). checked.label: 47 in 100 (how-withdrawal)
problems: 'expected' is not accurate. Bahji 2020: 'The overall pooled prevalence of CWS was 47% (6469 of 23 518)'; the abstract says it came from 'a random-effects meta-analysis model'. That is an average of 47 studies' observed rates, weighted. It forecasts nothing, so 'are expected to get withdrawal' reads as a prediction for the reader that the source never makes.

projection:true also makes the template show 'Worked out, not counted', not D6's 'Average across studies': projChip() picks 'Average across studies' only when x.pooled is true (SCHEMA.md 'pooled'). With projection:true, the weak text 'Average across studies' is stripped by PROJ_WORDS and never shown.

Right form: pooled:true, projection:false (rule 10's build check applies to projection only), and a past-tense headline. 'Averaged across dozens of studies' already says it is an average. 2 figures, 19 words, no verdict, no share-format error (checked with build_v3.py figs/wc/verdict/share_fmt). The head count of about 28 in 100 stays in basis.measured.

fix.numbers[10].headline: Averaged across dozens of studies, about 47 in 100 regular or hooked weed users got withdrawal when they stopped.

problems: Abstract (Europe PMC, refetched 2026-11-08): 'Long-term daily cannabis abusers (N = 25) who without treatment stopped using cannabis for at least one year'. The text and quote are right.

checked.label: step 3 (action 1 split; new felt proof)
problems: Action 1 split is D10 / r4-safety's text word for word. OK.

Proof figure checked against 08-v3/felt/cannabis.json with the graph's own merge (build_v3.py stage_meds, the same as one-pager-v3.html stageDots). Typical day per stage: Day 1 5 (29 posts), Days 2–3 5 (115), Days 4–7 5 (117), Week 2 4 (113), Weeks 3–4 3.5 (118), Month 2 3 (107), Month 3 3 (58), Months 4–12 3.5 (108), Year 2+ 1 (36). D9 headline that the template will compute: the peak is 5 and the highest later stage is 4, a difference of 1. That is a clear peak: 'Days 1–7: The hardest stretch. A typical day: 5 out of 10'. Easing: 'Weeks 3–4 … 3.5 out of 10'. One headline.

Wrong timing in the proof: 'after the first few days … 4 out of 10 or less' does not match the graph, which shows Days 4–7 at 5, inside the hardest stretch. The 4-or-less claim holds only from Week 2 (day 8) on. The draft's quote and 'via' use the raw 15 bins (Days 6–7 = 4), which the graph never shows. D9 says the proof must use the figure the graph shows.
The build's D9 check passes only because 4 is one of the graph's values (Week 2). It does not check the timing.

Fixed text: 2 figures, 25 words, no verdict (checked with build_v3.py figs/wc/verdict). 'after the first week' matches the graph's hardest stretch (Days 1–7), and action 3 ('Expect the first two weeks to be the hardest') still fits, since easing starts at Weeks 3–4.
